questions.q: A car travels at a constant speed of $66$ feet per second. What is this speed in miles per hour? ($1$ mile $= 5,280$ feet)
questions.answer: $\frac{66 \text{ ft}}{1 \text{ s}} \times \frac{3600 \text{ s}}{1 \text{ hr}} \times \frac{1 \text{ mi}}{5280 \text{ ft}} = \frac{66 \times 3600}{5280} = 45$ mph.

questions.q: On a map, $2.5$ centimeters represents an actual distance of $40$ kilometers. If two cities are $6.5$ centimeters apart on the map, what is the actual distance between them?
questions.answer: Set up a proportion: $\frac{40}{2.5} = 16$ km per cm. For $6.5$ cm: $6.5 \times 16 = 104$ km.

questions.q: A water hose fills a $120$-gallon tank in $15$ minutes. At this rate, how many gallons of water does the hose pump in $2$ hours?
questions.answer: Rate is $\frac{120}{15} = 8$ gallons per minute. In $2$ hours ($120$ minutes): $8 \times 120 = 960$ gallons.

questions.q: The price of an item was originally $80$. It was increased by $20\%$ and then the new price was discounted by $10\%$. What is the final price of the item?
questions.answer: Price after increase: $80 \times 1.20 = 96$. Price after discount: $96 \times 0.90 = 86.40$ dollars.

questions.q: A store manager discounts a winter jacket by $30\%$, making the sale price $84$. What was the original price of the jacket?
questions.answer: Sale price represents $70\%$ of original: $0.70P = 84 \Rightarrow P = \frac{84}{0.70} = 120$ dollars.

questions.q: In a chemistry lab, a $400$-milliliter solution is $15\%$ acid. How many milliliters of pure water must be added to dilute the solution to $10\%$ acid?
questions.answer: Amount of pure acid is $400 \times 0.15 = 60$ mL. In the new diluted solution with volume $400 + w$: $\frac{60}{400 + w} = 0.10 \Rightarrow 60 = 40 + 0.10w \Rightarrow 0.10w = 20 \Rightarrow w = 200$ mL.

sections.heading: Section 3: Scatterplots & Lines of Best Fit

questions.q: The line of best fit for a scatterplot relating weekly study hours $x$ to exam score $y$ is given by $\hat{y} = 4.5x + 52$. What is the predicted exam score for a student who studies $8$ hours?
For the model $\hat{y} = 3x + 25$, a student with $x = 6$ had an actual exam score of $47$. What is the residual for this data point?
In the linear regression equation $\hat{y} = -2.4x + 68$, where $x$ is the temperature in degrees Celsius and $y$ is the heating cost in dollars, what does the slope $-2.4$ represent?
choices: For each $1^\circ\text{C}$ increase in temperature, heating cost decreases by 2.40 dollars.
For each $1^\circ\text{C}$ increase in temperature, heating cost increases by 2.40 dollars.
The heating cost when temperature is $0^\circ\text{C}$ is 2.40 dollars.
questions.answer: The slope $m = -2.4$ indicates the rate of change: for every $1$ unit increase in $x$, $y$ changes by $-2.4$ (decreases by 2.40 dollars).

questions.q: A company surveys $200$ employees regarding remote work. If $120$ full-time employees and $80$ part-time employees participated, and $65\%$ of full-time and $40\%$ of part-time employees favor remote work, what percentage of all surveyed employees favor remote work?
questions.answer: Full-time favoring: $120 \times 0.65 = 78$. Part-time favoring: $80 \times 0.40 = 32$. Total favoring $= 78 + 32 = 110$. Percentage $= \frac{110}{200} = 55\%$.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a math competition is $5:7$. If there are $35$ boys, how many total students are in the competition?
questions.answer: Each ratio unit is $\frac{35}{5} = 7$ students. Total ratio units are $5 + 7 = 12$. Total students $= 12 \times 7 = 84$.

questions.q: If $x$ is inversely proportional to $y$, and $x = 12$ when $y = 6$, what is the value of $y$ when $x = 8$?
questions.answer: Inverse variation: $x \cdot y = k \Rightarrow 12 \cdot 6 = 72$. When $x = 8$: $8y = 72 \Rightarrow y = 9$.
